MESSAGE:
I run deliveries for a small furniture restorer and I've got a few things to sort for tomorrow.

Can you suggest a name for our new delivery van (staff vote, nothing rude)?

Tomorrow the van can't leave the depot before 08:30 and must be back by 12:00. Three drops, each takes 15 minutes to unload. Drop A has a delivery window of 09:00 to 10:00. Drop B is a shop that needs its delivery done before it opens at 09:30. Drop C is an office that won't accept anything before 11:00. Driving times: depot to A 30 min, depot to B 20 min, depot to C 45 min, A to B 25 min, A to C 40 min, B to C 50 min. The driver also needs a 30-minute break somewhere before 12:00. What order should he go in, and what's the timeline?

Could you also rewrite our delivery text so it sounds friendlier than "Driver arriving. Be in."? List three things the driver should check on furniture before handing it over. Should we give customers a paper delivery note or an emailed one? And define "proof of delivery" in a line for our new part-timer. One more thing: we're thinking of texting customers the evening before with a rough arrival time. Could you draft that evening-before text too, keeping it under 160 characters so it goes as a single message?

RESPONSE:
**Van name ideas for the vote:** Sofa So Good, Chester the Chest-Mover, Van Gogh, The Restoration Wagon, Dovetail Dave.

## Tomorrow's route: B → A → C

This is the only order that works:
- **A first:** you'd reach B at about 09:40, after it opens.
- **B, C, A:** C won't accept anything before 11:00.

| Time | What |
|---|---|
| 08:30 | Leave depot |
| 08:50 | Arrive at B (20 min drive) |
| 08:50-09:05 | Unload at B, before the 09:30 opening |
| 09:30 | Arrive at A (25 min drive), inside its 09:00-10:00 window |
| 09:30-09:45 | Unload at A |
| 10:25 | Arrive near C (40 min drive) |
| 10:25-10:55 | 30-minute break, parked up near C |
| 11:00-11:15 | Unload at C |
| 12:00 | Back at depot (45 min drive) |

There is no slack at the end. C can't start before 11:00 and the drive back is 45 minutes, so any overrun at C means a late return. The early part of the morning has about 35 minutes of float, so the driver should aim to be ready at C right at 11:00.

## Friendlier delivery text
"Hi [Name], your delivery from [Company] is on its way! Our driver will be with you around [time]. Please make sure someone's home to receive it. Thank you!"

## Evening-before text (under 160 characters)
"Hi [Name]! Your furniture delivery is pencilled in for tomorrow around [9-10am]. We'll text when we're close. Please make sure someone's in. - [Firm]"

That's about 150 characters with short placeholders. If your firm name or the time slot is long, check the final length before sending.

## Three checks before handing over furniture
1. **Condition:** Look for new scratches, chips, or marks, and confirm the finish is intact. Compare against your restoration photos if you have them.
2. **Stability and function:** Drawers, doors, and hinges should move properly, and legs and joints should be firm, with no wobble.
3. **Completeness:** Check that all parts, keys, shelves, and fixings are present, and that it's the right item for the right customer.

## Paper or emailed delivery note?
Email is the better default. It's easy to store and search, can't get lost, and can carry photos of the item's condition. Keep a paper copy as a fallback for customers who don't use email or when there's no signal. The driver should also get a signature or confirmation on the day either way.

## Proof of delivery
Proof of delivery is a record, usually a signature, photo, or timestamped confirmation, showing that the right goods reached the right customer in the agreed condition.
